answer: Operator collaterals per deed. Each identity submits a signed deed mapping operator to on-chain escrow at a shared atlas of operators; a wharf ledger records which operator deployed each clone, so sybils inherit their creator's exposure rather than the wallet's. When one wallet in a cluster defects or double-signs, the escrow behind every sibling on that ledge is slashed together, forcing the attacker to post full collateral for the entire fleet up front instead of per throwaway key.
